Gu Lingzhao's eyes grew even redder. Without a word, she turned aside and pulled a thick stack of silver notes from the wooden box, dividing them into two portions and shoving them into the hands of Nanqing and Nanyu respectively.

"Take these first; at the very least, don't let others profit."

The pitch-black, inky-dark midnight was no different from any other night, except that Mushui, the leader of the patrol guard, felt an inexplicable panic tonight, his eyelid twitching violently. As Ye Jing's personal bodyguard, such patrol duties shouldn't have fallen to him, but Ye Jing had been irritable lately and preferred to be alone. Furthermore, given that very few in this world could threaten Ye Jing with martial arts, Mushui had naturally become the captain of the estate's patrol guard.

"Lord Mushui, this subordinate feels something isn't quite right with Mingzhao Pavilion."

Hearing the name Mingzhao Pavilion, Mushui's heart gave an instant jolt.

"What is it?"

"In the past, at this hour, aside from the lanterns at the front gate, Mingzhao Pavilion was completely dark. But look, that large tree is faintly shimmering when the wind blows, yet the entrance is pitch black."

Mushui's gaze shifted toward Mingzhao Pavilion, only to feel his eyelid twitch even more violently.

"This subordinate is from the same hometown as Xunzun of Mingzhao Pavilion. How about I go knock on the door and ask? It'll be best if nothing is wrong, but if the Ninth Princess Consort blames us, we'll just say..."

Before the junior guard beside him could finish, a sudden, piercing shout virtually tore through the entire night.

"Someone come quick! Someone has escaped!"

Mushui immediately shouted, "You, take a few men and guard Mingzhao Pavilion. Everyone else, follow me."

The sound came from a small side gate of the Prince's residence. By the time Mushui rushed over with his men carrying lanterns, all he saw was a pale-faced Mulin and Nanqing lying on the ground in a pool of blood, her life or death unknown.

"Did you... do this?" Mushui doubted his own eyes; he was even praying this was a nightmare.

Mulin stomped his feet in anxiety, unable to speak clearly for a moment: "Th-this girl blocked the door and even tried to grab my sword, I also... never mind that, the Consort has escaped, what do we do?!"

"Why haven't you gone to report to His Highness?! If anything happens to the Consort, none of us will survive! You few, search the road toward the Marquis of Xuanping's estate, and remember to keep it quiet! Until His Highness issues an order, no one is to spread this word! Go!"

The guards scattered rapidly. Mushui looked at the person on the ground, clenched his teeth, and secretly carried Nanqing into a corner of the firewood shed.

Xuanwu Avenue, which led directly to the city gates, was the busiest and most bustling area in the capital by day. At midnight, stripped of the hustle and bustle of crowds, the entire street appeared vast and desolate. Tonight was exceptionally dark, as if a heavy rain was about to fall; the sky was as black as an abyss, the air oppressive and windless, weighing heavily upon people's hearts and causing quiet panic. The surroundings were eerily still, as if everything had been frozen and paralyzed.

Standing on this mandatory path leading to the Marquis of Xuanping's estate, Mushui and Mulin could feel the murderous aura emanating from their master. Ye Jing had not been in the residence tonight, and the back-and-forth had delayed a great deal of time. By the time he led the pursuit, there was no longer any trace of Gu Lingzhao to be found.

Cold sweat beaded on Mushui's forehead. The master before him had hardly spoken a single word all night, and he had a lingering premonition that something even worse might happen.

"Your Highness, ahead of us is the Xuanping Marquis's estate, but the Marquis's estate is currently guarded by the Imperial Army. Logically speaking, the Princess Consort shouldn't be able to get in."

Ye Jing merely tightened his grip on the sword at his waist and galloped toward the Xuanping Marquis's estate without a moment's hesitation.

"Your Highness! Breaking into a place guarded by the Imperial Army is a grave crime!"

Ye Jing abruptly halted his horse, and Mushui instinctively closed his mouth.

The sound of hoofbeats was exceptionally prominent in the quiet environment. A horse suddenly bolted out from the back door of the Xuanping Marquis's estate and galloped toward the city gate.

Those skilled in martial arts possessed heightened senses. With Ye Jing's prowess, no matter how dark the environment, it was little different from daylight to him. He saw the two figures on horseback with absolute clarity.

"Fetch my bow."

"Your Highness?!" Mushui and Mulin cried out in unison; their master must have gone mad!

chapters.title: Falling Off a Cliff
chapters.content:
"Stop talking nonsense!"

The long bow was handed into Ye Jing's hands. He drew the bow and nocked an arrow without the slightest trace of hesitation. His archery was peerless, hitting the target every single time without fail; he had absolute confidence that his arrow would not harm Gu Lingzhao, as he only wanted to force them to stop. Yet at the very last moment, Ye Jing suddenly remembered an official from the past who had fallen from a horse and died of his injuries. The fingers pulling the bowstring trembled inexplicably. Hesitating, that horse had already carried the two figures far away. Ye Jing closed his eyes, suppressing the raging fury in his heart.

"Prepare the horses!"

Seeing that they had reached the city gate while the sound of hoofbeats behind them drew closer and closer from afar, Nanyu, who had been controlling the reins all along, knew deep down that this horse carrying two people could never outrun the pursuers behind them, and the consequences of being dragged back by Ye Jing would be unimaginable.

"My lady, you must take good care of yourself in the future. Remember Uncle Liang's words: hold tight to the reins, head south to Wangyang Town, and forget everything here from now on."

"Nanyu..."

The space behind her became empty; Gu Lingzhao didn't even have time to catch a final glimpse of Nanyu.

After experiencing extreme terror, Gu Lingzhao suddenly felt as though a ball of fire inside her body was wantonly tearing through her internal organs.

Du Yufu hadn't lied to her this time; she had genuinely seen her father and witnessed the entire massacre of the Gu family.

Within the Xuanping Marquis's estate, she had witnessed a living purgatory with her own eyes. Blood and flames filled her vision, spilling over from a nightmare into reality. Hauled onto a horse by Uncle Liang and Nanyu, she didn't actually understand why she was running. Everyone was dead, what reason did she have left to live in this world?

Du Yufu's purpose was to subject her to the ultimate pain, leaving her with no desire to survive.

She had to admit Du Yufu had succeeded; for Gu Lingzhao, death was now the best destination.

Gu Lingzhao's horsemanship was mediocre at best. Now, in her daze, she couldn't even distinguish directions. The so-called escape was simply the horse running on its own while she instinctively clutched the reins. Before she knew it, she had galloped to the outskirts, completely unaware of her location. A fine, drizzly rain began to fall from the sky, and the night grew even darker.

The sound of hoofbeats behind her drew closer and closer, yet she remained utterly oblivious.

"Gu Lingzhao!" The roar coincided with a flash of lightning in the sky. Startled, Gu Lingzhao jolted, tumbled directly off the horse's back, and rolled down a high ridge several times.

It was Ye Jing!

They were in this together; they were all bad guys!

Only this single sentence echoed in Gu Lingzhao's mind. She could not fall into Ye Jing's hands! Absolutely not!!

Enduring the pain, she scrambled up with all her speed and ran forward. In the wilderness overgrown with weeds, the muddy ground was wet and slippery; Gu Lingzhao tripped and fell every few steps, only to drag herself back up from the mud. Her hands and face were scratched by weed blades into bloody trails, and the bruised spots on her body were countless.

Seeing this scene, Ye Jing was driven practically mad with fury. He couldn't understand what Gu Lingzhao was making a fuss about. Did she really need to run like a lunatic fleeing from wolves? Could he possibly eat her? In the entire capital right now, besides him, who else could protect her?!

"Your Highness, there seems to be a cliff just ahead!"

How could Ye Jing not know the danger of this place? Pulling his horse to a halt and reigning in his temper, he shouted as kindly as possible, "Stop running! I'm not chasing you. Come back now, and I can pretend tonight never happened!"

Yet this voice held not a shred of kindness in Gu Lingzhao's ears; she only felt that a demon was pursuing her from behind. Gripped by terror, she ran even faster.

"Your Highness!" Mushui cried out in warning.

Before his voice had even faded, Ye Jing was already executing his qinggong to catch up.

Gu Lingzhao could sense the presence of the person behind her. She had countless times rejoiced at his arrival, but now that familiar sensation brought her only despair.

Suddenly, her foot slipped. Following the immediate weightless sensation, before she even had time to scream, the world turned upside down, and her consciousness was snatched away.

"Zhaozhao!"

Ye Jing watched with his own eyes as Gu Lingzhao's figure suddenly vanished. His face turned pale, and his heartbeat seemed to stop abruptly.

"Zhaozhao..."

Ye Jing stared blankly at his own hand. His fingertips had clearly grazed Gu Lingzhao's clothing; just a fraction more, and he could have grabbed her!

Ye Jing instinctively took a step forward, only to be desperately pulled back by the guards who had rushed up from behind.

"Your Highness!"

The chilling rain fell upon his cheeks. In an instant, Ye Jing regained his composure. The patter of raindrops falling on grass leaves made a rustling sound, and the surroundings were as silent as death.

"Search. Regardless of the outcome, make sure you find her."

Ye Jing's voice was astonishingly steady, and his expression carried a calmness he had never shown in his past nineteen years.

On a pitch-black, rainy night, how easy could it be to search for someone at the bottom of a cliff? The cliff base was perpetually damp and covered in moss; merely walking was a challenge. A group of men searched all night, taking deep and shallow steps, yet failed to find even a shred of Gu Lingzhao's clothing.

Throughout the night, Ye Jing hardly uttered another word. As time ticked on, he felt increasingly cold, a chill radiating from the inside out.

He suddenly longed to hear Gu Lingzhao's voice. Mulling it over in his mind, he realized that his final interaction with Gu Lingzhao had been when he, consumed by fury, threw her onto the bed. She had seemed as though she wanted to speak to him then, but he hadn't listened...

Later on, Gu Lingzhao had also sent people to invite him, but he still hadn't gone...

Back then, what had she wanted to say to him?

He should have been a bit more patient with Gu Lingzhao; she wasn't very brave, and he shouldn't have left her alone in Mingzhao Pavilion... Nor should he have frightened her. If his voice had been softer just now, would she not have run so fast? Then he could have caught her...

Before he knew it, the rain gradually stopped, and the horizon began to grow faintly light.

Ye Jing gazed at the boulder-strewn bottom of the cliff, feeling as though a heavy stone had been dropped into his heart with a dull thud. Outsiders could detect no clue, nor did he feel any physical pain, yet occasionally, when he breathed, he felt a suffocating oppression in his chest.

By the second morning, several guards of Ye Zhang's appeared before Ye Jing with anxious expressions.

"Ninth Highness, we've finally found you. The First Highness wants you to return immediately. Something has happened!"

"I cannot leave at this moment. Apologize to my elder brother on my behalf."

"Ninth Highness, something major has happened! The Gu family is gone!" The messenger's voice pitched higher with anxiety. "Yesterday, a fire broke out at the Xuanping Marquis's estate, burning the entire Gu manor to ruins. Not a single one of the over a hundred people inside came out."

"What did you say? How is that possible!" Ye Jing's voice trembled with agitation, his chapped lips instantly seeping fresh blood.

"How would this subordinate dare to spout nonsense? The First Highness has been looking for you all day! The Fourth Highness spouted nonsense in the imperial court, insisting that the Marquis of Xuanping committed suicide by fire out of fear of crime, and the Third Highness started a fight right in front of His Majesty. The whole court is in absolute chaos! Right now, the only one left of the Gu family might just be the Ninth Princess Consort."

Just as the words fell, Ye Jing suddenly looked at him. The messenger was already sweating profusely from exhaustion, yet a biting chill blew into his heart in an instant. He felt a shivering cold down his spine under Ye Jing's ink-black pupils.

"Ninth Highness?"

"The rest of you stay here... I'll go back with you."

chapters.title: The Stunning Assassin
chapters.content:
In September of the twenty-third year of Zhengwu, the Xuanping Marquis's Mansion was charged with treason and colluding with the enemy. Gu Yi, the Marquis of Xuanping, committed suicide to escape punishment, and his son, Gu Lingfeng, perished with him in a sea of flames.

With this, the Gu family's foundation of a century was utterly destroyed to the ground.

In the winter solstice of the same year, the Xirong invaded the borders. The Ninth Prince, Ye Jing, volunteered to lead troops on an expedition. The grand army set out from the capital in the twelfth lunar month and rushed to the northwest.

In the summer of the twenty-fourth year of Zhengwu, the Fourth Prince, Ye Xuan, submitted a memorial impeaching Ye Tian for suspected treason, citing evidence of his collusion and communication with the Gu family. The Emperor was furious and placed Ye Tian under house arrest in his manor.

While framing Ye Tian, Ye Xuan also dispatched multiple assassins to murder Ye Zhang, ensuring that his path to seizing the legitimate succession would proceed unhindered, leaving him with no rivals.

However, in his complacency, he forgot the principle that even a cornered rabbit will bite.

Under the joint efforts of Ye Zhang and Ye Tian, a palace coup broke out suddenly.

That night, no one knew what truly transpired within the capital and the imperial palace. Outsiders only knew that overnight, the realm had changed masters.

The First Prince, previously obscure and unremarkable in the battle for the succession, was transformed into the ultimate victor. The Third Prince, formerly favored above all others, traded all his remaining influence for the status of an idle prince.

In August of the twenty-fourth year of Zhengwu, the Emperor passed away. In September, Ye Zhang ascended the throne as Emperor, changing the era name to Yuan'an.

Ye Tian was enfeoffed as Prince Jing, Ye Jing, far away in the northwest, was enfeoffed as Prince Rong, and Ye Xuan, previously the most arrogant and overbearing, vanished without a trace, disappearing so completely as if he had never set foot in this world.

---

The Third Year of Yuan'an

In a dense forest on the outskirts of the capital, a carriage was torn to pieces, its luxurious silks and brocades mixed inextricably with the mud. The air was thick with the stench of blood. Under the full moon, thick, crimson droplets of blood trickled down the blood-groves from the tip of an ancient dark-iron saber.

"D-Don't kill me! What do you want? I can give you silver. Whatever those people paid to hire you, I'll give you double, ten times!" Lou Changgui collapsed onto the ground before the man in black, pleading with a trembling voice. He wanted to flee, but his legs were too weak to support him. The corpses scattered haphazardly around him were all elite guards he had hired at a high price. Lou Changgui had guessed beforehand that the road into the capital would not be peaceful, but he never imagined that anyone would actually dare to intercept and assassinate a court-appointed official on the outskirts of the capital! And a single person at that, who had slaughtered their group of over twenty without giving them the slightest chance to fight back.

A ferocious and menacing Taotie mask was worn on the assassin's face, making him look like a murderous demon stepping forth from the netherworld. Seeing that blood-stained saber drawing closer and closer, Lou Changgui let out a shriek of utmost terror: "I am a court-appointed official! My elder brother is a third-rank senior official in the imperial court! If you harm me, my brother will not let you go!"

Upon hearing this, the assassin paused slightly. From behind the terrifying mask came a scoff, a cold female voice as crisp and frigid as the snow waters of the Cangshan Mountains: "Lord Lou need not prove his identity. If I didn't recognize you, why would I have come to kill you? Rest assured, your elder brother will soon be joining you down below."

"You! What on earth are you?! Don't kill me, I beg you, taking innocent lives will bring retribution."

"When you framed and poisoned General Gu Sheng, wrongfully taking the lives of his two sons, did you ever think about the retribution of today!"

"You're here to avenge the Gu family?" A chill pierced straight through his entire body. In Lou Changgui's mind, only a single thought remained: It's over!

"It seems your intelligence isn't very well-informed. Look at your elder brother; a month ago, he fled to the capital and has been hiding behind closed doors ever since." The assassin was not in a hurry to make a move; the night was still long, and for enemies, letting them die too quickly was also a form of mercy.

"What do you want to make you spare me? In the matter back then, we were just following orders. My elder brother is a protégé of Prime Minister Du; if you touch me, Prime Minister Du will not stand idly by! I..."

"Prime Minister Du?" At the mention of this name, the assassin was instantly enveloped in an aura of bloodlust, losing all patience to listen to Lou Changgui's nonsense. "Since you admire Du Hongzhi so much, then go wait for him down in the Yellow Springs to protect you."

A cold flash flickered, and a head rolled on the ground with a dull thud. All the struggles and words of the dying ultimately transformed nothing more than a pair of eyes wide with unresisting resentment.

The morning sun rose, and the capital was bustling with churning crowds, presenting a lively and prosperous scene.

"Why is the capital so lively today?" a neatly dressed young girl asked a middle-aged man carrying a carrying pole, who looked eager to join the crowd.

The man's face was full of smiles, and he answered with great enthusiasm: "Today is the day Prince Rong returns in triumph to the capital! Prince Rong has been on campaigns for four years, pacifying both Xirong and the Southern Frontiers in one stroke. He is the true God of War of our Great Qian! If we can catch even a glimpse of his esteemed countenance, it would be a blessing cultivated over several lifetimes for us commoners!"

The girl smiled politely, watched the man's cheerful retreating figure, and then turned to walk toward a teahouse.

On the second floor of the teahouse, a veiled woman in plain robes sat by the window. She gazed quietly out at the street, her eyes seemingly frozen with millennia of unmelting ice.

This place was near the city gate rather than the bustling market district, and this teahouse was a common lodging place for martial artists of the jianghu. The woman possessed an extraordinary bearing, her eyes resembling lotus flowers in cold water, carrying a captivating and soul-stirring beauty.

"Master, listening to the words of the townspeople, Prince Rong's victorious procession is entering the capital today," Qingyu trotted up, standing to the side and respectfully reporting.

The woman gently lowered the teacup in her hand. The outer rim of the cup collided with the scabbard of the ancient saber lying horizontally across the table, producing a crisp sound. It was precisely this blood-stained blade that made many who wished to strike up a conversation recoil in hesitation.

Her gaze never left the window. Outside was a wonderfully lively scene, with commoners crowding both sides of the street. Even with the scorching sun directly overhead, no one left, everyone's eyes filled with curiosity. That look of excitement and anticipation was just like when she had first sat waiting for Ye Jing to return to the capital all those years ago.

Returning to this teahouse after many years, Gu Lingzong no longer felt uneasy in her heart due to the mixed company of all sorts of people.

"I can tell by the two maidens' attire that you are not locals. I am Zhou Li of the Chiyan Gang. I wonder if I might have the honor of making the acquaintance of the two maidens."

Zhou Li familiarly took a seat opposite them, following Gu Lingzong's gaze to look out the window.

"Is the maiden also hoping to witness the demeanor of the God of War? You perhaps do not know, but this God of War of ours is the biological younger brother of the current Emperor, and also the youngest son of the Empress Dowager. It wouldn't be an exaggeration to say his power reaches the heavens now. But when it comes to martial arts, I simply don't believe that this pampered young master possesses any real skill."

Qingyu was young and detested arrogant and conceited people the most. She rolled her eyes from the side, disgust lacing her tone: "A moment from now when Prince Rong passes by here, jump out of the window and spar with him, then you'll know his skill."

Zhou Li stared intently at Gu Lingzong and asked, "Would the maiden like to take a look?"

chapters.title: Prince Rong Returns to the Capital
chapters.content:
"Zhou Li, don't end up dragging this entire teahouse down just to win a beauty's smile! Prince Rong grew up on Mount Cangsu, studying under sect leader Yu Shanyuan. The martial arts he practices are different from those of other aristocratic young masters. Don't talk about just you; even if your entire Chiyan Gang swarmed him together, you wouldn't be a match for Prince Rong."

"What business is it of yours? The young lady hasn't even spoken yet." Zhou Li did not abate his wild arrogance, his eyes fixed straight upon Gu Lingzong's veil, as if impatient to pierce through the thin gauze and see the true face beneath. "This maiden, might you do me the favor of telling me your honorable name and where you reside? Consider it making a friend. Jianghu people are all in the capital, so we can look out for each other in the future."

Gu Lingzong finally cast a proper glance at his way and said softly, "South Xiao Tower, Dragon-Tiger Pavilion."

South Xiao Tower, the largest assassin organization in the contemporary jianghu, gathered a group of the most ruthless martial arts masters who regarded human lives as nothing more than grass.

Rumor had it that as long as there was enough gold, there was no contract in this world that South Xiao Tower dared not accept.

Upon hearing this, Zhou Li's expression instantly froze. Stiff-tongued, he asked, "You are people from South Xiao Tower? Uh... this younger brother has some miscellaneous matters to attend to, so I won't disturb your refined tastes any longer. Farewell!"

Zhou Li fled at top speed. When the surrounding people caught wind of the three words "South Xiao Tower," they too hurriedly retracted their gazes from Gu Lingzong.

"Arrogant and brainless, yet he runs fast enough." Qingyu sneered, pulling her legs up to sit by the table, resting her chin on her hand as she asked in a low voice, "Master, is Prince Rong's martial arts really that good? Compared to the Tower Master, who is stronger?"

"We've never crossed swords; there's no way to judge... Did you hear the drums? They are entering the city."

Before the army reached the city gate, the sound of beating drums already resounded across the earth. Inside the city, the Feathered Forest Guards stood on both sides of the road to maintain order, yet the awe-inspiring soldiers were no match for the enthusiasm and curiosity of the commoners. They had heard of Prince Rong's great military achievements, but none could recall what this young God of War actually looked like.

At the head of the procession atop a tall steed, Ye Jing was clad in dark-gold armor, wearing a golden crown with dark hair, his posture straight and upright. Years of campaigning had completely stripped away his former youthful air; now, his facial features were more sharply defined, and his pair of phoenix eyes held a natural authority that did not require anger to terrify. Merely gazing at him from afar was enough to inspire involuntary awe.

The commoners lined both sides of the road, their eyes shining as they looked at the God of War riding the tall steed at the front of the army. The men felt admiration, while many of the maidens directly blushed.

Prince Rong had spent four years on the border, fighting from Xirong all the way to the Southern Frontiers, recapturing nearly a dozen cities in one stroke. Such a military record was virtually unprecedented since the founding of Great Qian, and Ye Jing was only just over twenty years old. Returning to the capital in victory naturally made him the center of attention for the entire city.

"Ah! So this is Prince Rong! Truly as jade-like a branch of a tree, handsome and dashing!"

"They all say Prince Jing is as handsome as Pan An, but I think Prince Rong is hardly inferior. What immense blessings must one cultivate in their past life to be able to marry Prince Rong as a wife?" several maidens exclaimed in the crowd.

"I heard the Empress Dowager has already bestowed a marriage, and the chosen one is Du Yufu, the legitimate eldest daughter of the Prime Minister's Estate."

"No, that's not right. How come I remember that this Prince consort once took a wife? You forgot, the eldest miss of the Xuanping Marquis's Mansion used to be the number one beauty in the capital, and she was drop-dead gorgeous."

"Shh, keep your voice down. The entire Gu family is dead; don't bring up past matters."

"I know, I didn't dare speak loudly. If you ask me, Prince Rong is rather ruthless. Such a gorgeous beauty died young less than half a month after their marriage, and it seems even her bones were never properly buried in the end... Do you think this Prince might be somewhat cursed to lose his wives? Um..."

"Hurry and cover her mouth, before the one left without even bones remaining is us."

A few young girls in the crowd were chatting and laughing amongst themselves when they suddenly felt a chill in the surroundings. Looking up, they abruptly realized that the high and mighty God of War was glaring sideways at them.

That look could hardly be called kind. Even though he merely glanced at them for a fraction of a second, it still sent a bone-chilling cold straight from the depths of their hearts.

Scared ashen-faced, the girls only dared to speak again once the procession had marched far away.

"With such a distance away, Pr-Prince Rong shouldn't have been able to hear what we said, right?"

"I'm scared. I want to go home..."

No one paid attention to this little interlude, save for the fact that Ye Jing's expression turned even colder, lacking any of the self-satisfaction of a triumphant return.

Indeed, Ye Jing had never experienced the sensation of sudden fame and being pursued by thousands. In the past, relying on favor, Ye Xuan had been arrogant and tyrannical by nature, intolerant of anyone whose achievements surpassed his own. He found it difficult to heavily offend Ye Zhang and Ye Tian, but bullying Ye Jing carried no scruples at all, and he had stolen goodness knows how many of Ye Jing's merits out in the open.

The year they suppressed bandits in the outskirts of the city, Ye Jing's injuries were glaringly visible. Yet in the end, it was the person who hadn't even held a sword hilt who calmly accepted all the congratulations from every quarter.

The Emperor didn't care; Imperial Concubine De was entirely focused on her eldest son; and court ministers were even less likely to cast their gaze upon a useless person.

There was only one person who, in private, would meticulously apply medicine to him with eyes full of heartache, offering gentle and soft words to console his disappointment.

"How can wiping out bandits be considered a great military achievement? In the future, my A-Jing has the ability to become a commander-in-chief. Recovering lost territory and protecting the peace of a region; that is what can truly be called a military exploit."

"You think I can?"

"Naturally. You are, after all, the person with the best martial arts and the greatest courage I have ever seen. Actually, I was right there in the teahouse without a signboard by the city gate today. It's a pity you didn't even spare me a single glance! Simply unforgivable!"

The voice in his memory was gentle and soft, lacking the imposing momentum even when trying to bluff.

"Considering that you're injured, I won't hold it against you. But next time, you aren't allowed to miss seeing me."

"Alright. If there's an occasion like this next time, I will definitely be able to spot my Zhaozhao at first glance."

A sharp pain pierced his chest, and Ye Jing snapped back to reality in an instant. Along this entire journey back to the capital, those memories that had almost faded began to grow like wild grass fed by the wind, occupying his mind inch by inch.

A teahouse by the roadside came into Ye Jing's line of sight. It felt as though his heart had been ruthlessly squeezed; his eyes could no longer register anything else, and in a trance, everything around him became unreal.

As he reached the foot of the teahouse, he raised his head, staring unblinkingly, scanning window by window to search for a person who could not possibly be there.

A light breeze blew, and Ye Jing's gaze was suddenly drawn by a flash of white. However, in the blink of an eye, there was nothing behind that window anymore.

"Master, just now Prince Rong turned his head and looked toward this side!" Qingyu did not understand why her master had sat here staring for so long, only to hide her figure behind the window the moment Prince Rong passed by.

"Did you see? The God of War actually has quite a handsome face."

"Let's go."

Gu Lingzong picked up her saber, uttered a single word, and rose to walk downstairs.

chapters.title: The Death of Lu Qin
chapters.content:
"Master, Prince Rong just turned and glanced over here!" Qingyu didn't understand why her master had sat here staring for so long, only to hide her figure behind the window the moment Prince Rong passed by.

"Did you see that? The God of War actually has quite a handsome face."

"Let's go."

Gu Lingzhao picked up her saber, uttered a single word, and rose to walk downstairs.

Qingyu hurriedly packed her things and followed.

The two hastily left the teahouse, but before reaching their lodging, they encountered an uninvited guest in a deserted alley.

The long saber carried by the newcomer was very similar in shape to the one Gu Lingzhao held, but what was more eye-catching was his striking head of red hair. Chiyu wore a smile at the corners of his mouth, but those pale pupils stared fixedly at Gu Lingzhao, carrying a hint of a fight to the death.

"The reputation of my Dragon and Tiger Pavilion isn't something just any stray cat or dog can use."

Qingyu showed a look of indignation and immediately retorted, "You're the stray cat and dog, you ginger freak!"

"Qingyu." Gu Lingzhao softly stopped Qingyu, looked at Chiyu, and explained, "My coming to the capital this time is solely to pursue a personal grudge; I will not get in your way. You and I can mind our own business."

"Hmph! Honeyed words! You crazy woman, using my favorite long saber to blatantly murder imperial officials in the outskirts of the capital; I see you're clearly trying to use a borrowed knife to kill!"

Qingyu stepped forward, her momentum completely unyielding against Chiyu: "Ginger freak, what kind of wronged party are you acting like? Last year in Jiangnan, you visited seven brothels in three days, and you even used the name of our Vermilion Bird Pavilion! You should consider yourself lucky we didn't sell you to a pleasure house to be a kept boy."

"Stinking girl, you're looking for death!"

"As if this mistress is afraid of you!"

"Enough!" Gu Lingzhao barked, cutting them off.

"Chiyu, what on earth do you want?"

Chiyu narrowed his eyes at Gu Lingzhao and said with an unfathomable expression, "What do I want? Unfettered Wind, taking advantage of the Pavilion Master's secluded cultivation to enter the capital without an order; you truly don't put the Pavilion Master in your eyes at all."

"The Pavilion Master has given an order." Chiyu raised a dark red jade token, his voice solemn. "He commands the Dragon and Tiger Pavilion and the Vermilion Bird Pavilion to retrieve the Phoenix Blood within a month. Disobedience will be severely punished."

Gu Lingzhao's brows furrowed slightly at these words. The Phoenix Blood was a sacred healing artifact, rumored to have the power to bring the dead back to life and grow flesh on bones. She had been searching for it in secret all these years, but had never found any trace.

"The Pavilion Master is urgently seeking the Phoenix Blood. Is he injured?"

"That is not for us to know." Chiyu walked closer to Gu Lingzhao, his tone chilly. "I know that if we fail to get our hands on this Phoenix Blood, both of you and I will likely take a tour of the Serpent Cave... Ah, look at my memory, I almost forgot that our Vermilion Bird Pavilion Master is a regular visitor to the Serpent Cave."

"Cut the crap. Within a month, how easy is it to find the Phoenix Blood like finding a needle in a haystack?"

"I already have a lead on the Phoenix Blood. Follow me..."

Gu Lingzhao glanced at Chiyu, then turned to instruct Qingyu, "Go back first. Follow the plan and scope out the Lou residence first."

"Understood, Qingyu understands."

Gu Lingzhao followed closely behind and to the side of Chiyu. The two walked through the dark alleys of the market quarter, yet always maintained a certain distance, an unspoken precaution between two top-tier assassins.

"You certainly have a lot of nerve, daring to be so audacious right in the imperial capital."

"I merely killed a minor local official, not like Pavilion Master Chi, who dared to strike a high-ranking second-grade official of the imperial court."

Thinking of past events, Chiyu's complexion turned somewhat ashen: "That fellow was just unlucky, hiding so deeply that even the most well-informed intelligence post of the South Xiao Tower couldn't uncover his identity..."

Chiyu seemed to recall something, suddenly stopping in his tracks to look at Gu Lingzhao: "You were there back then too. Could it be that you knew all along that the fellow surnamed Lu was truly a high-ranking minister of the court?"

It was no wonder Chiyu still harbored resentment. If he hadn't committed a major taboo against the imperial court in the first year of Yuan'an and been hunted down by the government for several consecutive years, he wouldn't now be sitting on equal footing at the South Xiao Tower with Gu Lingzhao, an assassin who had entered the trade midway.

Gu Lingzhao replied indifferently, "Someone whom even you couldn't investigate; how could I possibly have the ability of foresight?"

Back then, someone offered ten thousand taels of gold to kill a Confucian scholar in the capital. But it was right at the time of the new emperor's ascension, and the imperial city was heavily guarded; killing someone in broad daylight was far too reckless, and Chiyu wasn't someone with too many lives to spare, so he had gone to some trouble to abduct the man to a secluded spot, intending to dispose of him quietly.

Yet that Confucian scholar was no incompetent either. Taking advantage of the guards' inattention, he pressed his back against the sharp brick edges and literally sawed through the rope binding his hands. In the end, though he failed to escape, he earned an opportunity to speak with Chiyu.

The man directly revealed that he was a second-grade official of the current court; if Chiyu would spare him, he promised thousands of gold in gratitude later. The South Xiao Tower was actually unwilling to have too much confrontation with the court; if this man truly was a second-grade official, Chiyu might have actually spared his life.

Yet the strange part was that Chiyu had people investigate for a whole night and still failed to uncover the Confucian scholar's true identity. Later, when dawn broke, Chiyu lost his patience and slit the man's throat on the spot.

For Gu Lingzhao, who had observed the whole process, she was actually more than clear about the man's identity.

Though she hadn't met Lu Qin many times, she would never, under any circumstances, forget his scheming old face!

She had to admit, the feeling of coldly watching others writhe in the agony of life and death was truly quite pleasant.

Actually, counting it up, Lu Qin and Gu Lingzhao didn't have a direct, irreconcilable blood feud; he had simply made the choice most favorable to himself under the circumstances of that time.

Therefore, Gu Lingzhao returned the favor in kind. She stood by and watched as Lu Qin had his throat slit directly by the impatient Chiyu because his identity could not be verified, remaining completely silent throughout and not uttering a single extra word. Droplets of fresh blood splattered onto her dress, failing to stir up the slightest ripple in her heart.

The reason Chiyu couldn't investigate Lu Qin's identity was very simple: as Ye Zhang's confidant, Lu Qin had never been officially registered as an official in the court for many years, concealing his identity with extreme thoroughness. And after Ye Zhang ascended the throne, although he had promised Lu Qin a second-grade official position, the imperial edict had not yet been issued, so Lu Qin remained a mysterious figure in the capital.

In just that back-and-forth time gap, Chiyu had brought this monstrous disaster upon himself.

Lu Qin died, the Emperor flew into a rage, and the South Xiao Tower underwent a catastrophe. The Xuanwu Pavilion was completely wiped out, the Azure Dragon and White Tiger Pavilions were each half destroyed and merged into today's Dragon and Tiger Pavilion, still entrenched in the northern capital region. As for the Vermilion Bird Pavilion, it was later taken over by Gu Lingzhao, with its forces mostly concentrated in the Jiangnan region.

Chiyu led Gu Lingzhao to an ordinary residence. He guarded closely against Gu Lingzhao; naturally, he would not bring this grave threat to the stronghold of the Dragon and Tiger Pavilion.

"Take this map." Once inside the room, Chiyu immediately tossed a scroll to Gu Lingzhao.

Gu Lingzhao opened the map and glanced at it for just a few moments before immediately looking up to ask, "Is this a map of Prince Rong's estate?"

Chiyu raised an eyebrow in surprise. "You certainly know your stuff."

Gu Lingzhao's knuckles trembled slightly and involuntarily: "...You mean the Phoenix Blood is in Prince Rong's estate?"

"Precisely. The Phoenix Blood was once a sacred artifact of the Southern Frontier. Someone witnessed with their own eyes Prince Rong taking the Phoenix Blood into his own possession when he exterminated the Southern Frontier imperial family. Prince Rong's victorious army is entering the capital at this time, and the palace banquet will end no earlier than the Hour of Hai. You and I will strike tonight and infiltrate Prince Rong's estate by night!"

chapters.title: She Is Not My Gu Lingzhao
chapters.content:
With an exceptionally solemn expression, Chiyu couldn't help but mock, "What? Scared? Weren't you very spirited when admiring the demeanor of the God of War today? If we have good luck, you might even have a chance for intimate contact tonight."

"...I will accompany you to infiltrate the estate by night today. If we can obtain the Phoenix Blood, you must not obstruct me when I seek revenge in the capital in the future."

"Alright, it's a deal!"

---

Inside the imperial palace, Ye Jing first paid respects to the reigning emperor, and was then immediately urged to go to the Empress Dowager's Feng'an Palace.

"Jing'er, let Mother look at you!"

With tears in her eyes, the Empress Dowager reached out to stroke Ye Jing's face, saying, "You've grown thin, and taller too. The borderlands are bitter and cold, mostly wind and sand. My son has suffered; now that you've returned this time, do not leave again."

"Your son is doing very well at the border and hasn't felt it to be a hardship." Ye Jing forced a smile. Even though they were mother and son by birth, facing the Empress Dowager's intimacy, it was hard for him to muster a corresponding expression.

When Ye Jing was three years old, because a Daoist priest asserted that he and Ye Zhang were ill-matched and would bring mutual harm, he was sent away to Mount Cangsu by his mother, only to be welcomed back to the capital when he was fourteen. At that time, it was the critical moment of the struggle for the succession, and Imperial Noble Consort De was entirely devoted to Ye Zhang, even deliberately distancing herself from him.

Ye Jing understood his mother's predicament; she had her difficulties. He had never blamed his mother and still respected her, but if she wanted to demand anything more from him, he was simply powerless to comply.

Seeing the stiffness in his expression, a flash of disappointment crossed the Empress Dowager's eyes.

"I know you find the borderlands free and easy, but the capital is no longer what it used to be. With Mother here, from now on you may act entirely according to your own wishes in the capital." Before Ye Jing could reply, the Empress Dowager immediately added, "The banquet is about to start, go take your seat. From now on, every day for you and me, mother and son, will be a day of reunion."

With the Empress Dowager speaking thus, it effectively sealed Ye Jing's lips. He thought over and over again, and in the end said nothing more.

Banquets in the palace were always unoriginal, consisting of nothing more than string and wind instruments, song and dance, accompanied by flattery over raised cups. For Prince Rong's welcome banquet, all court officials of the third rank and above, along with their families, were present. Sweeping one's gaze across the grand hall, it was filled with gorgeously dressed aristocratic sons and daughters.

Ye Jing raised his eyes to look around. The grand hall was as peaceful and prosperous with song and dance as ever, and the faces exchanging cups among the seats were all familiar ones. Having left Shangjing for four years, he had originally thought there would be earth-shaking changes after the dynastic shift, but in reality, things were far from the vicissitudes of life he had imagined.

The only change was probably the swapping of his and Ye Tang's seats; he was now the imperial prince with the highest status in the entire court.

No longer would anyone ignore his words; everyone's gaze converged on him, and the voices of flattery were endless.

Today was a celebration banquet, and cups were crossed amidst the festivities, making it seem as though everyone were happy. Yet Ye Jing could feel no joy whatsoever; he could not blend into this cheerful atmosphere. Looking at the smiles on people's faces, he only found them unfamiliar and even repellent.

Ye Jing sat in the seat of honor, lowering his eyes, and only replied briefly when Ye Zhang asked questions. Anyone with discerning eyes could see that Ye Jing was in a bad mood, but they truly could not figure out why this prominent and battle-tested young prince was feeling so gloomy. The official in charge of organizing the banquet couldn't help but pound drums in his heart, wondering where things had gone wrong to displease His Highness Prince Rong.

However, if it came to looking grim, there was indeed one other person in this grand hall who could rival Ye Jing.

Before the title of the God of War, if one spoke of the most renowned figure in the imperial family, it would be none of other than Prince Jing, Ye Tang. The exceptionally handsome Third Highness back then; even if his status was not what it used to be, whenever Prince Jing was mentioned, people's eyes would still light up, and they would not stint on praise for that former favored son of heaven.

Yet at this moment, Ye Tang, who had always been known for his magnanimity and gentleness, had a complexion noticeably worse than Ye Jing's. The two sat directly opposite each other, each one more unhappy than the other.

The courtiers were also helpless. Who didn't know that Prince Rong had an unapproachable personality in his youth? Back when he had no backing, he had dared to rely on sheer reckless drive to fight Ye Xuan, who wielded the most flourishing influence at the time. Ever since news of Prince Rong's impending return to the capital, they had known that an ancestor-like figure was returning.

No matter what, however, Prince Jing was the one who had truly been wronged back then. A set of loophole-ridden charges had caused the Marquis of Xuanping's estate to be wiped out overnight, and the Gu family was nearly exterminated entirely. Anyone with a shred of conscience left in their heart could not help but sigh when mentioning the tragedy of that year.

In the grand hall, apart from those few families who used to walk closely with Ye Tang, more people still could not figure out why Ye Tang, who had always been renowned for his gentle temperament, would glare so hostilely at Ye Jing. Could it be that he disliked today's seating arrangement? Or was he dissatisfied that this role of universal adoration now belonged to someone else?

The tune of the string and wind instruments suddenly changed, melodious and lingering like affectionate murmurs. A woman covered her face with both sleeves, gracefully moving with lotus steps as she slowly approached, dancing lightly. With her graceful posture and light footsteps, everyone in the hall held their breath, as if immersed in a dance of a celestial being.

At first, Ye Jing didn't care; he didn't even raise his head to look.

Until the dance ended, the Empress Dowager, sitting in the high seat, clapped in praise and said, "Miss Du's dancing posture is truly the best in the capital. Looking at it, Aijia feels refreshed and relaxed. Jing'er, don't you think so?"

Ye Jing pulled back his thoughts, raising his head just in time to meet Du Yu-fu's bashful pair of eyes.

Another pair of eyes suddenly surfaced before him, sorrowful, desolate, and agonizing. He recalled her crying; the weeping was ethereal yet seemed to come from all directions, gripping his throat and making it hard for him to breathe.

"Jing'er? You're staring with your eyes wide open. Aijia just asked you how you think Miss Du's dance was," the Empress Dowager said with a smiling expression.

"Since Mother says it's good, naturally it is good."

"You child... Yu-fu's dance was exhausting, quickly take your seat."

"Thank you, Your Majesty Empress Dowager." Du Yu-fu curtsied to the figures in the high seats. Whether it was intentionally arranged or not, her seat was right to the right hand of Ye Jing.

"How come I didn't notice before? Looking at Prince Rong and Miss Du like this, they truly are a match made in heaven." Liang, the Imperial Uncle, knowing the Empress Dowager's intentions, boldly bantered under the influence of alcohol. Besides, Ye Jing couldn't possibly publicly reject the face of his own maternal uncle.

Yet Ye Jing was, after all, Ye Jing; worldly human sentiments were merely a word in his heart.

Only to see Ye Jing raise his eyes to stare fixedly at Imperial Uncle Liang, his gaze, tempered in seas of blood, like a falcon's, sending a chill down Imperial Uncle Liang's spine.

"Years have passed, Uncle, your eyesight might be failing, or perhaps your memory is poor. Take a good look; this is not my Gu Lingzhao. I am not well-acquainted with Miss Du, so Uncle had better refrain from making such joking remarks."

chapters.title: My History with Her Needs No Interference from Outsiders
chapters.content:
The moment those words left his mouth, the entire courtyard plunged into a dead silence. Prince Liang's face drained of color, and he froze on the spot.

Expressions varied among the onlookers, but astonishment predominated. In their understanding, the cause of Eldest Miss Gu's death remained a mystery, but based on subsequent events, it was not hard to guess that her tragic demise was inextricably linked to Ye Jing.

If Gu Lingzhao had been murdered by someone else, given Ye Jing's previously demonstrated undying love for her, he would have already turned the capital upside down, found the killer, stripped their skin, torn their tendons, and scattered their ashes to the winds.

Gu Lingzhao's fate had even secretly become a cautionary tale among the aristocratic households, warning young ladies of noble birth that a man's affections should not be lightly trusted.

That year, such a passionate and earth-shattering love had still failed to withstand fame, fortune, and political power. One moment they were the envy of all, and the next she was a withered skeleton in the netherworld.

Previously, the official families and noble consorts of the capital had universally agreed that the name Gu Lingzhao must now be a taboo for Prince Rong. But looking at it now, one could only conclude that His Highness Prince Rong was unfathomable, or perhaps had reached the pinnacle of ruthlessness, utterly indifferent to the past.

"Jing'er, that is your uncle!" The Empress frowned, a trace of displeasure evident in her voice.

"It is this son's fault. The alcohol went to my head and I offended my uncle. I hope my uncle will not hold it against me." Ye Jing stood up and bowed to the Empress. "This son will go outside to sober up first. Please forgive me, Your Majesty and Mother Empress."

With that, he walked out of the banquet hall without looking back, leaving a crowd of officials looking at one another in dismay.

Ye Jing walked all the way to the lakeside and placed his hand on the railing. In truth, he hadn't touched a single drop of alcohol, yet waves of dizziness washed over him.

"Gu Lingzhao..."

Uttering that name aloud in the great hall startled even Ye Jing himself. Over the past four years, no one had ever dared mention that name in his presence, and even he himself had come to feel that those three syllables were distant and unfamiliar. Yet, when the words reached his lips, there hadn't been the slightest hesitation, as if that name had already been caressed and whispered tens of thousands of times deep within his heart.

He stood in the corridor pavilion, looking dazedly out at the lake, only to turn and see Ye Tang standing not far away.

Ye Jing tilted his head slightly, his hand resting on the white stone railing, and said in a flippant tone, "Third Brother, long time no see. Trust you have been well?"

In front of Ye Tang, a peculiar sense of competitiveness always stirred within him, even though Ye Tang had never wronged him in any way.

Perhaps it was because of the betrothal between Ye Tang and Gu Lingzhao, or perhaps because he knew Gu Lingzhao truly appreciated Ye Tang. Even though he had later snatched her away by force, he always felt that in her heart, he somehow fell a notch short compared to Ye Tang.

"Not a match for Ninth Brother's elegance," Ye Tang replied coldly. He truly could not be bothered to put on pretenses with Ye Jing.

"In all these years of knowing Third Brother, I have never seen you look at anyone with such an expression."

"I simply have no tolerance for despicable and base villains."

"Despicable?" Ye Jing let out a light snort, his tone laced with mockery. "Third Brother has always prided himself on being a man of noble and upright character. Can you guarantee that your own hands are entirely clean? Has Third Brother truly never used unscrupulous means for his own selfish desires?"

A blazing fury ignited in Ye Tang's eyes. He stepped right up to Ye Jing and said through clenched teeth, word by word, "Using unscrupulous means should still have a limit. Struggles between men, whether overt or covert, are all just methods. But you had no business dragging an innocent woman into this! You used every trick to defraud Ah-Zhao of her sincerity, putting on a devoted act to fool all of us. She was only seventeen back then! How did Ah-Zhao treat you in the past, and how did you treat her?! Have you never felt a shred of guilt all these years? In the dead of night in your dreams, aren't you afraid she'll come back to claim your life?!"

Hearing this, Ye Jing threw his head back and laughed, his phoenix-like eyes brimming with evil charm. "Whether Gu Lingzhao is dead or alive, she is still my wife. Whatever grievances exist between her and me need no interference from outsiders. On what grounds are you leveling accusations against me?"

"I am Ah-Zhao's cousin! She is a younger sister I watched grow up since childhood!"

"Though your maternal clan belongs to the Gu family, Marquis Gu was not your biological uncle. In terms of bloodline, you and Gu Lingzhao are not even remotely related. If Third Brother feels he has too much free time on his hands, why not spend more time with Third Sister-in-law?"

"You!" Ye Tang had not expected anyone in this world to be so utterly shameless. A raging fire surged in his heart, and he raised his fist to strike Ye Jing.

"Husband! You must not!" Mu Yunyao rushed out from somewhere and tightly grabbed Ye Tang's arm. "Today, all the civil and military officials are gathered in the great hall; you must not act rashly!"

"We were just speaking of Third Sister-in-law, and here she is." Ye Jing smiled and greeted Mu Yunyao. Seeing her stern expression, he added with a punch-able grin, "Sister-in-law has arrived just in time. Please manage Third Brother and keep him from meddling in other people's family affairs."

"Ye Jing! You are a cold-blooded and shameless villain!"

Ye Tang had always been a kind-natured man who valued the demeanor of a gentleman, rarely losing his temper in front of outsiders. At least in Ye Jing's memory, he had never seen Ye Tang lose his composure like this.

"Third Brother's temper seems to be getting worse. In the past, you were always the one among us brothers who loved self-cultivation and restraint." Ye Jing still refused to rein it in, as if he were determined today to goad Ye Tang into throwing a massive scene. "Sister-in-law, do not hold Third Brother back. Whatever anger he has, he can direct it right at me. What if he ends up bottling it up and hurting his health later?"

Mu Yunyao swept a cold glance over Ye Jing, then turned and earnestly pleaded with Ye Tang, "Husband, if Ah-Zhao were to see you plunging yourself into trouble over a matter like this, she certainly would not wish it... Calm yourself, and do not let small matters ruin the bigger picture."

Looking into Mu Yunyao's meaningful gaze, Ye Tang lowered his eyes in prolonged thought before finally extinguishing his anger. He gave Mu Yunyao a gentle nod to signal that he had calmed down.

Watching this husband and wife display such tacit understanding, trading glances back and forth, Ye Jing suddenly could not smile anymore. Raising his eyes, he caught sight of the gold headwear inlaid with red rubies on Mu Yunyao's head. Under the dim, yellowish palace lanterns, those red rubies, which ought to have been dazzling and bright, looked to Ye Jing like dark red bloodstains, stirring a dull, aching bitterness deep within his chest.

He remembered this very set of headwear... Gu Lingzhao had given it to Mu Yunyao as a wedding gift before Ye Tang's marriage...

Mu Yunyao had once been one of Gu Lingzhao's best friends. As high-born noble daughters carefully nurtured by their respective aristocratic families, the two of them even bore a striking resemblance in many ways.

Now that Mu Yunyao was standing upright and poised before him, it gave Ye Jing a deeply hallucinatory illusion... As if his Gu Lingzhao should also be somewhere nearby, and if he only searched with all his heart, he might still be able to hold her hand once again.

"His Highness Prince Rong has returned victorious from the frontier, and my husband and I ought to offer our congratulations."

Ye Jing forced a smile and replied, "We are all family brothers, why must Sister-in-law be so formal?"

"His Highness Prince Rong is currently reveling in his triumph, yet you should also remember that in this world, there is still the law of karmic retribution; that what goes around comes around. Of course, if Your Highness believes your actions have been open, above-board, and clear of conscience, then naturally you need not care about my words."

"Sister-in-law truly lives up to your reputation as a renowned talented woman of the capital." Ye Jing loudly applauded. Being arrogant by nature, he was accustomed to putting up a stiff front and would never lower his head by even a fraction. "I have never believed in ghosts and gods. As for retribution, this prince would just as soon like to see what these deities and Buddhas actually look like, and what they could possibly do to me."

chapters.title: Assassins on the Roof
chapters.content:
Disregarding the murderous look in Ye Tang's eyes entirely, Ye Jing smiled and prepared to walk past the couple. As he brushed shoulders with Ye Tang, he heard him suddenly drop his tone into one of flat calm: "Ah-Zhao was naturally shy. Having known her for many years, she only ever proactively sought me out in private once."

Ye Jing did not stop walking immediately; he had a gut feeling that the other man was not going to say anything he wanted to hear.

"At that time, you were confined to your residence, and she came to beg me, asking me to find a way to smuggle her into the palace for a trip. She wanted to see you. Back then, I was quite astonished by her audacity..."

Ye Jing's steps halted abruptly. His legs felt as though they had been filled with lead, refusing to lift another inch.

"Ye Jing, I truly can do nothing against you. True justice is hard to find in this world. Back then, Marquis Gu was not entirely unaware of that impending disaster; it was simply that events moved too quickly. All he could do was hurriedly choose someone who could protect Ah-Zhao's peace and safety for the rest of her life. You put on an act too flawlessly, at the time, Marquis Gu genuinely believed you could protect her life."

Ye Tang let out a long sigh, figuring that Ye Jing probably couldn't understand his words anyway.

"Actually, you needn't worry that Ah-Zhao will take revenge on you. Knowing her personality, she would surely never want to see you again in her next life."

Ye Jing clenched his fists tightly. His lips moved; he wanted to refute, to strike back, but the other man's few casual words possessed the terrifying force of a roaring mountain torrent, crushing the facades and self-deceptions he had built up in his heart with the momentum of a collapsing dynasty.

He finally felt a trace of fear. He did not want to hear another word from Ye Tang. He walked away with extreme haste, looking very much like a man fleeing in panic.

The couple did not linger long in the palace, taking their leave early under a pretext.

When Ye Jing returned to the banquet, he accepted every toast offered to him without refusal, maintaining the posture of someone determined to drink until he collapsed. Seeing how heartily he was drinking, the guests flattered him all the more. Before the banquet had even officially concluded, Ye Jing was already too drunk to walk steadily.

In the end, the gathering had to be ended early so that Ye Jing could return to rest as soon as possible.

Leaning crookedly inside the carriage, Ye Jing heard nothing in his ears except Ye Tang's accusations echoing over and over.

With wide-open eyes, he stared blankly at the roof of the carriage. He thought to himself that he wasn't afraid of Gu Lingzhao coming back for revenge. It was just that when she was alive, her health had never been robust; even if she turned into a ghost, she'd likely be a weak one. Otherwise, why hadn't he dreamed of her even once in all these years?

Could it really be as Ye Tang said; that she despised him to the core, and therefore never wanted to see him again?

No, no... Ye Tang must be talking nonsense. It must be because he had been stationed too far away that Gu Lingzhao couldn't find him.

The journey was eerily quiet, save for the sound of carriage wheels grinding over stone pavement.

Ye Jing closed his eyes and thought that perhaps she didn't necessarily have to become a ghost. If he couldn't dream of Gu Lingzhao, maybe it was because she wasn't actually dead; how could a living person ever visit someone in a dream?

A flicker of hope seemed to ignite in his heart, and Ye Jing couldn't help following that train of thought: If Gu Lingzhao was alive, where would she be? Did she truly hate him to the marrow of her bones? He had known Gu Lingzhao for so many years, yet he had never known what she looked like when she hated someone...

The one advantage of the bitter, freezing borderlands was that they forced a person to focus only on the immediate moment; the constant, ongoing battles were Ye Jing's best excuse for forgetting the past.

Yet now, he no longer had any excuses to fool himself, leaving him no choice but to let his thoughts grow wild like creeping vines until his mind was entirely filled with the silhouette of Gu Lingzhao.

The carriage stopped in front of the Prince's Manor. Mushui called out twice from outside, and seeing no movement within, assumed Ye Jing had fallen asleep inside. To his surprise, when he lifted the carriage curtain, he found himself staring straight into Ye Jing's pitch-black eyes.

"Your Highness..." Mushui was startled. Before he could react, Ye Jing nimbly vaulted down from the carriage.

"Your Highness, take it slow." Catching the smell of alcohol on Ye Jing, Mushui hurriedly stepped forward to support him, only to be shoved aside.

"Step aside. This prince isn't crippled to the point where he can't even walk."

Helpless, Mushui stepped back, but the next moment, he was yanked forward again by the collar.

"Mushui, did you know? Gu Lingzhao... she's still alive..."

Mushui's heart gave a violent jolt, and he stared at Ye Jing with shock in his eyes.

"Are you saying the Princess Consort is still alive? Did His Highness the Prince of Jing tell you this?"

Back then, Ye Tang had also dispatched men to search the bottom of the cliff, so Mushui felt that the possibility of Gu Lingzhao being rescued by Ye Tang wasn't entirely zero.

"No, I just feel that with so many people from various factions living well in this world, why would the heavens alone demand her life?"

Hearing Ye Jing's ethereal, drifting words, Mushui secretly swallowed hard. His Highness repeatedly bringing up the Princess Consort... this was by no means a good sign.

Sure enough, Ye Jing's next seemingly casual self-questioning nearly frightened him out of his wits.

"If Ah-Zhao is truly dead, then why am I still living in this world?"

"Your Highness, you must be drunk! Someone come, quickly help His Highness inside!"

A group of guards swarmed forward instantly, practically carrying Ye Jing through the gates of the manor.

"Mushui."

"This subordinate is here."

"Look at that roof over there. There seems to be an assassin." Surrounded by guards, Ye Jing spoke in a casual, teasing tone, devoid of any seriousness. Mushui's heart skipped a beat. He looked in the direction Ye Jing was pointing, but the distant rooftops were pitch black; nothing could be seen.

Thinking nothing of it, Mushui was about to say there was nothing there when suddenly, a patch of emerald-green light flared in the darkness, and the green radiance genuinely cast the silhouette of a person.

"Men! There's an assassin! Catch the assassin!"

Inwardly cursing his terrible luck, Chiyu thought running straight into Ye Jing returning early was bad enough, but why did that jade-green roof tile lamp have to light up at this exact cursed moment?!

The manor guards swarmed from all directions. Standing atop the roof beams, the assassin had no choice but to draw his sword and respond.

The men Chiyu selected to follow him naturally possessed formidable martial arts, but facing Prince Rong's guards, who had clawed their way out of the battlefield, he lost momentum. Under a flurry of flashing blades and drawn swords, he was forced back step by step.

Hiding behind Chiyu, Gu Lingzhao urged in a low, hurried voice, "Quickly signal your men to withdraw immediately!"

"Since we've run right into them, we might as well test the foundation of this Prince Rong's Manor."

"You're courting death..." Gu Lingzhao reached out anxiously, but failed to grab the eager Chiyu.

In the blink of an eye, Chiyu leaped up onto the roof. Other Dragon and Tiger Pavilion assassins hidden in the shadows also vaulted onto the rooftops to clash with the manor guards.

The two sides fought to a standstill, and the entire Prince Rong's Manor was instantly filled with the ringing clash of weapons.

Gu Lingzhao concealed herself behind a tall wall. From her angle, she had a clear view of Ye Jing's tall, slender figure from the side.

They were very close; Gu Lingzhao could even clearly see the look of pure intrigue plastered across Ye Jing's face.

As Ye Jing tilted his head to watch the combat, he genuinely felt that this spectacle was far more entertaining than the string and wind music and singing dances of the imperial court.

chapters.title: Direct Confrontation
chapters.content:
"The Prince's guards need to drill more. It takes them this long just to take down a few assassins? You go, make it quick."

"Yes!" Mushui's voice turned stern as he drew his sword and plunged into the fray.

As the Prince's top-tier bodyguard, Mushui's skill was plain for all to see, and his entry immediately broke the stalemate. Chiyu blocked a strike from him, and the web of his thumb instantly went numb, almost causing him to drop his weapon.

Chiyu's expression shifted drastically; he never imagined that a mere guard could possess such prowess.

In that momentary daze, dozens of blades slashed down right at him. Chiyu frantically raised his saber to parry, but the subtle feeling of his arms losing strength gradually bred a sense of ominous dread in his heart.

"Are you still not going to make a move?!"

Before the words faded, Gu Lingzhao appeared as if out of thin air. Her long saber was unsheathed, and with a mid-air slash, the rushing wind carried an overwhelming momentum, snapping the long swords of half the guards in a single strike.

She moved across the rooftop as if walking on flat ground, sweeping her leg to directly kick three guards tumbling down.

Chiyu was similarly shaken by Gu Lingzhao's ferocity. "Not bad, your skills have improved..."

Gu Lingzhao shot him a fierce glare, her Taotie mask failing to conceal her anger.

If she hadn't been worried that this red-haired freak would blurt out something he shouldn't if captured by Ye Jing, she would have had to be out of her mind to come and rescue him!

With her residual anger unappeased, Gu Lingzhao's next strike came straight down at Mushui, blade and sword clashing to throw off a shower of sparks.

Mushui could not stop himself from retreating, a shock rising in his heart as he hadn't expected this sudden interloper to possess such formidable internal energy.

"Make it quick!"

"Alright!"

Chiyu dared not linger any longer and began actively coordinating his attacks with Gu Lingzhao.

The two fought as they retreated, waiting only for the right moment to flash away.

Seeing the two attempt to escape, Mushui dared not slacken in the slightest, ordering the others to deal with Chiyu while he leaped forward to block Gu Lingzhao's retreat.

Yet after exchanging several consecutive blows, Mushui grew increasingly strange in his heart; the opponent seemed able to anticipate his moves a step in advance. Before he could dwell on it, sword techniques laden with internal force had already forced him into a defensive crouch.

Gu Lingzhao swept out with her left palm, unleashing a wave of energy that cleared the roof tiles beneath Mushui's feet. Taking advantage of Mushui's unsteady footing, she spun around, intending to use qinggong to escape. However, the surrounding air suddenly twisted. Gu Lingzhao first saw Chiyu get struck down off the roof by a single palm, and immediately after, a terrifying force enveloped her in an instant.

With no time to react, she instantly discarded her saber and channeled all her internal energy to meet it.

Palm met palm in a massive clash of internal force, scattering turbulent currents of air that blew the other people on the rooftop straight down.

Taking that palm head-on was no easy feat. Gu Lingzhao retreated dozens of steps, hooking the roof beasts on the edge of the eaves with her toes to barely stabilize her body and keep from falling.

Ye Jing stood tall and upright upon the ridge of the roof. The night was windless, the moonlight grew thicker, and between heaven and earth, it seemed only the figures of the two standing in opposition were reflected.

"A bunch of trash!" Ye Jing glanced downward, deeply displeased. Shifting his gaze back to the person before him, for some reason, upon seeing this figure, a faint pain pulsed in Ye Jing's heart, spasming to the point that even his breathing grew restricted.

However, he didn't pay it much mind, shaking his head and chalking it up to having had too much to drink.

"You've got some nerve, stirring up trouble in this Prince's territory. Surrender yourself and explain your intentions clearly, and this Prince might spare half your life."

Gu Lingzhao raised her eyes to look at the person before her. This was the first time in four years she had directly faced Ye Jing in broad daylight, or rather, face-to-face. Ye Jing had not changed much from the appearance in her memory, and those phoenix eyes still held the unbridled arrogance most familiar to her.

In the past, she had countless times looked up at those eyes. This exact distance was just enough for the former Ye Jing to run over and hug her... A squalid past like shattered pieces of glazed glass pierced fiercely into her heart.

Gu Lingzhao raised her hand to channel her internal energy, summoning the ancient saber that had fallen onto the roof tiles back into her hand. She raised the saber, its edge pointing straight at Ye Jing.

"Incorrigible." Ye Jing sneered, a murderous intent flashing through the depths of his eyes. He suddenly grew very interested, eager to see what kind of face lay beneath that fierce beast mask.

Ye Jing's movement technique was extremely fast, and in a flash, he was right before her. Gu Lingzhao slashed down with her saber, but the blade was blocked by internal energy, feeling as though it had chopped into cotton. Thinking to herself that this was bad, she tried to retract the move, but Ye Jing spun his body, pressing in close, and directly clamped down on the wrist holding her saber.

Gu Lingzhao lunged forward, slamming her shoulder into Ye Jing to use his momentum against him. At the same time, she released her right hand and shifted the blade to her left hand.

Just as Ye Jing's gaze followed her long saber, Gu Lingzhao suddenly exerted a fierce burst of force, breaking free from his grip. A miniature dagger unexpectedly materialized in her right hand, thrusting straight for Ye Jing's throat.

Though Ye Jing dodged with sufficient promptness, a trace of pain still flared at his neck.

Gu Lingzhao knew full well Ye Jing's strength and vicious nature; she could never afford to engage in close combat with him. Having no time to dwell on it, her other hand morphed from a palm into a claw, scratching toward Ye Jing's face.

"Want to ruin my face?"

Ye Jing dodged effortlessly, spinning around to easily grab Gu Lingzhao's other arm. Standing tall and built with a commanding frame, his posture made it look as though he were embracing her.

In an instant, cold sweat broke out all over Gu Lingzhao; this person was far stronger than she had guessed.

She dared not imagine the consequences if her identity were discovered by Ye Jing...

Their bodies pressed together, close enough to feel each other's heartbeats. Ye Jing clearly saw that beneath the ghost mask were a pair of watery autumn eyes filled with fear; a pair of eyes that seemed extraordinarily familiar to him.

Ye Jing felt as though he had been struck over the head with a club, his mind going completely blank for an instant.

Memory and reality overlapped. Ye Jing had long since forgotten where he was, and he dazedly reached out his hand, wanting nothing more than to tear off this mask.

Seeing him exposed in a moment of vulnerability, Gu Lingzhao's tense nerves suddenly relaxed. She immediately took a step back, and without any hesitation, twisted her body to deliver a heavy knee strike straight to Ye Jing's chest.

The dream shattered abruptly. Ye Jing let out a muffled grunt, his footing giving way as he fell backward off the roof.

"Your Highness!" The guards on the ground were startled and scrambled to catch him, none of them expecting Ye Jing to be injured so easily.

When a person falls from a height, the scenery before their eyes slows down drastically. A mere instant for others was enough for Ye Jing to contemplate many things. He didn't feel it was shameful for a dignified God of War to be ambushed by a little assassin and tumble off his own roof. He was simply wondering if he really was drunk, to actually see the shadow of Gu Lingzhao in that assassin's eyes.

The crowd from the South Xiao Tower scattered and fled in the chaos. Chiyu closely followed behind Gu Lingzhao. Once they reached a safe area, he wanted to say something to Gu Lingzhao, only for the latter to stop in her tracks the very next moment, spin around, and deliver a heavy punch straight to his abdomen.

Chiyu was hit so hard he immediately doubled over, unable to even string together a curse for a moment.

"...What the hell are you going crazy for?!"

chapters.title: Handing You Over to Prince Rong's Manor
chapters.content:
"I figured you might not know what pain feels like, so I came specially to remind you!" Gu Lingzhao was currently burning with rage. After being startled and terrified, she simply couldn't restrain her fury! "Next time you want to seek death, leave me out of it!"

"Bufeng, stop putting on an act here! Which person who treasures their life would become an assassin? If we don't test Prince Rong's true strength today, how can we make plans for the future?"

"And how did your test go, then?"

"Since the Azure Tile Lamp lit up, it proves that the Phoenix Blood is indeed in Prince Rong's estate... Judging by that Prince Rong's martial arts, going toe-to-toe is probably out of the question."

Chiyu looked at Gu Lingzhao, who was standing with her arms crossed, then suddenly walked closer and without warning raised a hand to snatch off her mask.

"This face of yours might still have some use. Don't look with such a fierce gaze; who knows, perhaps Prince Rong might also break his back for a beauty like you." Chiyu spoke with a smile, completely oblivious to the danger. "How about I send you into Prince Rong's estate? I heard Prince Rong still doesn't have a single female confidante..."

Gu Lingzhao narrowed her eyes, and the next instant, she kicked out straight at Chiyu's vital spot.

"Ugh..." Chiyu collapsed onto the ground, in too much pain to speak, and could only glare round-eyed to accuse Gu Lingzhao of her viciousness.

"He doesn't have women around him, which might just mean he likes men. Why don't you go test the waters yourself first? Prince Rong might just take a fancy to you out of sheer novelty!"

"You!"

"I already went with you to probe Prince Rong's estate. If the Dragon and Tiger Pavilion dares to obstruct my affairs again in the future, don't blame me for being merciless." Dropping these words, Gu Lingzhao paid no more attention to Chiyu's expression, picked up her mask, turned around, and vanished alone into the boundless dark night.

Gu Lingzhao owned a heavily concealed courtyard in the capital, and those who knew of this place were all her true confidants.

Returning to her own room, Gu Lingzhao casually tossed the mask aside and sat heavily down on a pearwood chair, breathing deeply and heavily. Sweat dampened the stray hairs on her forehead, making her look like a fragile white jade porcelain vase, beautiful yet untouchable.

"Master!" Seeing Gu Lingzhao's poor complexion, Qingyu immediately poured a cup of warm water and handed it to Gu Lingzhao, asking anxiously, "Was the operation a success?"

Gu Lingzhao shook her head and said wearily, "We crossed paths with Prince Rong and nearly lost everyone in there. However, the Azure Tile Lamp lit up, confirming the location of the Phoenix Blood, so it wasn't a wasted trip."

Qingyu said incredulously, "Even a joint effort between you and the red-haired freak didn't work? Can this Prince Rong's strength pierce the heavens?"

Gu Lingzhao didn't want to dwell too much on tonight's events. She changed the subject and asked, "We don't need to rush the Phoenix Blood, but Lou Changfu must be butchered as soon as possible. How is the investigation into his whereabouts? Have you figured out his recent movements?"

At the mention of this, Qingyu's anger flared even higher: "This old fox is terrified of death. Ever since he fled back to the capital, he hasn't stepped foot outside his estate's gates. The Lou family's residence in the capital is right next to the Capital Magistrate's office, and Lou Changfu has hired plenty of guards. The brothers staked the place out for several days and only saw layers upon layers of guards. Master, why don't you let me take a few people to charge straight in and hack that old codger to death!"

"You just said it yourself, the Lou estate is right next to the Capital Magistrate's office, right under the emperor's feet, yet you want to forcibly break into an imperial official's home to kill someone." Gu Lingzhao gave Qingyu a deep look. "Lou Changfu isn't worth us all going to throw our lives away."

Gu Lingzhao rubbed her temples, raised her head to look at the distressed Qingyu, and said, "You've worked hard these past few days, go get some rest first."

"Master..."

"Step down."

"Yes."

As Qingyu left, she gently closed the room door.

Through the half-open window, Gu Lingzhao gazed aimlessly outside. It was the third watch of the night, a pitch-black darkness where one could not see their own hand.

She could often perceive fate toying with her. Perhaps the heavens felt she had committed too many sins over the past few years and, to torture her, was finding every possible way to entangle her with Ye Jing.
